claim_verdicts.evidence: git show stage-0:.../PlaceOrderLong.cs: 10-16 early returns; 18-22 `totalVnd += line.Quantity * line.UnitPriceVnd;`; 24-27 `if (customerIsLoyal) { totalVnd -= totalVnd * 10 / 100; }`; 29 `totalVnd += totalVnd >= 2_000_000 ? 0 : 30_000;` (fee only when < 2,000,000); 31-32 two Console.WriteLine (saving, email); 34 `return $"order placed, total {totalVnd}";`.

Line 26 `totalVnd -= totalVnd * 10 / 100;` mutates totalVnd in place; line 29, the next statement, compares that same totalVnd with 2_000_000. Execution (claim 3) confirms: 10% -> fee added (2010000), 5% -> no fee (2090000).

Ran it: scratch net10.0 console copying PlaceOrderLong.cs verbatim from stage-0 plus a copy with `* 5 / 100`, input new OrderLine(2, 1_100_000), customerIsLoyal=true. Output: "order placed, total 2010000" and "order placed, total 2090000" (saving lines print the same totals).

Lines 4-5: `// One method that checks, prices, saves and notifies. Four reasons to change` / `// one place, and no name for any of the four.` The lesson quotes the second sentence verbatim. Note: the comment sits above `public static class PlaceOrderLong` (line 6), not directly above the method (line 8) — see issue on section 5.

Definitional/opinion with a stated condition; no pinned-version document governs it. Lesson wording (§3 "together shape how expensive later changes are", §9 "a large part of what later changes cost") is hedged and consistent with the ledger. No docs opened for this claim.

After line 26, totalVnd is read on line 29 (fee), 31 (`saving order for customer {customerId}, total {totalVnd}`) and 34 (return). Line 32 is `Console.WriteLine($"sending an email to customer {customerId}");` — customerId only.

Inspected whole file at stage-0: the only comment (lines 3-5) says nothing about which total the fee uses; no variable or method names the original vs discounted total — there is only `totalVnd`, overwritten on line 26 before line 29 reads it. Statement ordering alone decides it.

Opinion with condition; follows from claims 2 and 6. "by accident" keeps it true: a fee rule given the discounted total as a named input would still change on a discount edit, but visibly, not by accident. No external source applies.

issues.quote: a one-character pricing edit reached the shipping fee
issues.text: Carried over from round 1, still unfixed here (§2 was fixed to "tiny edit"). Changing `10` to `5` replaces two characters with one; it is not a one-character edit. Unlisted factual claim.
issues.fix: Replace with "a one-number pricing edit reached the shipping fee" (and the vi equivalent).

issues.text: Unlisted evaluative claim, and it clashes with §8, which says the prerequisite lesson read `PlaceOrderLong` "for its length" (as too long). A junior sees the two lessons disagree.
issues.fix: Replace with "`Place` reads top to bottom with no tricks, yet" — or drop "short and".

issues.quote: The file's own comment, just above the method, names the problem
issues.text: The comment is on lines 4-5, above `public static class PlaceOrderLong` (line 6); the method `Place` starts on line 8. It is above the class, not the method.
issues.fix: Replace "just above the method" with "just above the class" (or "at the top of the file").

issues.quote: If each rule took the value it needs as a named input, a discount edit could not reach the fee by accident
issues.text: I paused here: if the fee rule took the discounted total as its input, a smaller discount would still remove the fee. I cannot quite reconstruct why it would no longer be 'by accident'. I guess the point is that someone would have to choose which total to pass, but the sentence does not say so.
issues.fix: Add a clause after 'by accident': 'because whoever passes the input has to pick, by name, the original or the discounted total — the business decision becomes visible in the code'.

issues.quote: The file's own comment, just above the class, names the problem: "Four reasons to change one place, and no name for any of the four."
issues.text: Neither code block (lines 8-22, 24-34) shows this comment, so I looked for it and could not find it. The prose quotes it, so I am not stuck, only briefly distracted.
issues.fix: Add 'which is not in the blocks above' after 'just above the class', or drop 'The file's own comment, just above the class,' and keep only the quoted sentence.

issues.quote: design — the choices about where each piece of work lives and what it can reach
issues.text: 'what it can reach' in the definition means what a piece of work can read (variables). Sections 4-6 use 'reach' for a different thing: what a change reaches ('a discount edit could not reach the fee'). Two meanings of one verb made me re-read.
issues.fix: Replace 'what it can reach' with 'which variables it shares with other work'.

issues.quote: - reason to change — a rule the business might ask you to change on its own
issues.text: The three Core concepts entries are not bolded, unlike terms in the prerequisite lessons' Core concepts, so they did not stand out as the terms to remember when they reappear later ('reason to change' in section 4, 'change cost' in the Try it answer).
issues.fix: Bold the three terms: **reason to change**, **change cost**, **design**.

issues.quote: asks why their shipping fee disappeared
issues.text: Working it out, the customer now pays 2,090,000 instead of 2,010,000 — more, not less. A customer asking about a fee that vanished (in their favour) felt a little odd until I did the maths; the stronger surprise is that the total went up.
issues.fix: Change to 'asks why their total went up by 80,000 VND when only their shipping fee changed' or 'asks why their shipping fee disappeared yet they paid more'.

issues.quote: The fee is decided from `totalVnd` after the discount has already changed it, so a smaller discount can lift the total over the threshold
issues.text: Carried over from round 1: option a is about twice as long and more specific than b, c, d; I could pick it by length alone. c ('recompiles', 'cached value') is obviously off-topic.
issues.fix: Shorten a to 'The fee line reads `totalVnd` after the discount has changed it', or make b and d as long and specific.

issues.quote: False, because passing tests only shows today's behaviour; it says nothing about how much a later change will have to touch.
issues.text: Better than round 1, but 'today's behaviour' still echoes summary line 4 ('tests describe today's behaviour') and section 6 ('what the code does today'); I can match it by words.
issues.fix: Anchor c in the example: 'False: `Place` passed before and after the discount edit, yet the edit still changed the fee nobody meant to touch.'

issues.quote: The notification still sits in the same method as checking, pricing and saving, so adding SMS still means editing and re-checking all of it.
issues.text: Carried over: only a is plausible and it is the longest; b, c, d are easy to reject. Also 'editing … all of it' overstates — I would edit one line near the email line and only re-read the rest.
issues.fix: Change to 'still means reading and re-checking all of it', and make one wrong option plausible, e.g. 'Renaming makes the email line easier to find, which is all the SMS change needs.'

issues.quote: Renaming would matter when it changed behaviour, but a rename done consistently leaves results identical
issues.text: Carried over: the 'would matter when … were' pattern in the b, c, d explanations reads oddly; I had to re-read each to get the point.
issues.fix: Use 'if': 'Renaming would matter if it changed behaviour, …'; same for c ('if the question were') and d ('if readability were').
